blocks.text: Re: Engagement for a Patent Portfolio Review
Dear Mr. Smith:

You have asked us to review the patents and patent applications held by {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} and to tell you, family by family, which of them justify the cost of keeping them in force and which do not. This letter confirms that engagement and records its scope, the people who will carry it out, its start date and fee, and the terms on which we will act for you, and it becomes our agreement when you sign and return the signature page.
The Review

We will review the issued United States patents and pending United States applications that the company owns, together with their foreign counterparts, and we will organize the work by patent family so that related filings are assessed together. For each family we will report its legal status, its remaining term and the maintenance fees or annuities that will fall due over that term, the state of the recorded chain of title, and how its claims, as issued or as pending, relate to the products the company sells or intends to sell.

The review ends in a written report, marked privileged, that makes a recommendation for each family: maintain it as it stands, seek further protection through a continuation or another filing, or allow it to lapse at its next payment date. Each recommendation will state the information on which it rests and the facts that would change it.
What the Review Does Not Cover

The review is not an opinion that any patent is valid or enforceable, and it is not an opinion on whether any product, the company's or a competitor's, infringes any patent; each of those is a separate opinion that requires its own investigation and its own engagement letter. Preparing new applications, responding to office actions, and representing the company in any dispute are also outside this engagement, although the report will say where the review suggests that one of those steps deserves your attention.
Order of Work

We will begin by reconciling the company's docket against the records of the United States Patent and Trademark Office and the relevant foreign offices, because every later conclusion depends on knowing which matters are alive and which dates are open. We will then take the families in order of their nearest payment or response deadline, and anything we find that cannot wait for the final report will be brought to you in writing as soon as we find it.

To do this we will need the company's own docket records, its file copies for each family, the assignment and employment agreements signed by the named inventors, and a current description of its products and product plans. We will ask for all of it in a single written request in the first week of the engagement, so that you are not answering piecemeal.
Who Will Do the Work

Heather Munoz, a Partner in our prosecution group, will supervise the review and sign the final report, and every legal conclusion in that report will be hers. Kelly Snyder, a registered Patent Agent, will review the prosecution histories day to day and will be your usual point of contact, and Amanda Schwartz, an Associate, will examine the chain of title for each family and map the claims against the product information you provide.

I remain responsible for the firm's relationship with the company, and you should call me directly if anything about the engagement itself, as distinct from the substance of the work, is not as you expect.
Conflicts of Interest

Before sending this letter we searched our records for any representation adverse to {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} and found none. If a conflict comes to light during the review, we will tell you in writing at once and will not proceed on the affected matter until it is resolved.
Start Date and Fee

Work under this letter will begin on {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}, provided we have received the signed signature page by then, and we expect the review to take about seven months from that date. The review is undertaken for a fixed professional fee covering the scope described above, and that fee is set out on the signature page that accompanies this letter.

Official fees charged by the patent offices, the charges of foreign associates, and similar costs are not part of the fixed fee. We will bill them at cost and will ask before incurring any that are not routine.
Fees and Payment

We will invoice the fixed fee in monthly installments over the expected term of the review, and costs in the month in which they are incurred, and each invoice is payable within thirty days of its date. If an invoice remains unpaid sixty days after its date, we may suspend work on written notice to you, and if it remains unpaid thirty days after that notice we may withdraw from the engagement, subject to our obligations under the rules of professional conduct.

Suspension or withdrawal will never be the means by which a deadline goes unattended. Before we stop work for nonpayment, we will send you a written list of every open deadline in the portfolio that is known to us, in enough time for you to make other arrangements.
Term and Termination

This engagement runs from the start date until we have delivered the final report and answered your questions on it, and it then ends without further notice unless we have agreed in writing to continue. Either of us may end it earlier by written notice, in which case the company will owe the portion of the fixed fee that corresponds to the work completed by the date of the notice, together with any costs already incurred.

Reviewing the company's docket does not make us responsible for maintaining it. Whether during the review or after it ends, we will monitor deadlines, pay maintenance fees or annuities, or take any action before a patent office only on your written instruction for the matter concerned.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence everything the company gives us in the course of this engagement and will use it only for the review. Our communications with you and the report itself are intended to be protected by the attorney-client privilege, and to preserve that protection we ask that you limit their circulation to the people within the company who need them and that you speak to us before sharing them with anyone outside it.
Limitation of Liability

Our recommendations will be professional judgments based on the public records and on the information the company provides, and we cannot guarantee how any patent office, court, or competitor will act on any matter in the portfolio. We are not responsible for consequences that follow from information that was withheld from us or was inaccurate when given, or from decisions the company makes against our written advice.

Nothing in this letter limits our liability to the company for our own professional negligence. The rules of professional conduct do not permit a lawyer to limit that liability in advance unless the client has separate counsel advising it on the point, and we have not asked you to do so.
Governing Law

This letter is governed by the law of the state in which this firm maintains its principal office, without regard to that state's rules on conflicts of law. Together with its signature page it is the entire agreement between us on this review, it replaces our earlier discussions on the subject, and it may be changed only in a writing signed by both of us.
If these terms are acceptable, please sign the signature page and return it to me, and Kelly Snyder will send the document request in the week the work begins.
Very truly yours,
Kickoff Memorandum
Objective

The review opened on {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}. We owe the client one recommendation per patent family: keep it, extend it, or let it lapse. Each recommendation rests on the record and states what would change it.
The client contact is Gary Smith, General Manager. He reads the conclusion first. Every family summary opens with its recommendation.
Order of Work

items: Docket reconciliation. Sharon Woods compares the client's docket with USPTO and foreign office records. Every open date goes on our docket as a reminder. We act on a date only on the client's written instruction.
Chain of title. Amanda Schwartz checks the recorded assignments for each family. She also reads the inventors' assignment and employment agreements. Gaps go on her issues list with a proposed fix.
Prosecution and claims. I take the families in order of nearest deadline. For each one I record status, remaining term, payment dates, and claim scope.
Product mapping. Amanda Schwartz maps the claims to the product information Gary Smith sends. Where his description is thin, we ask him. We do not fill the gap ourselves.
Recommendation and report. Heather Munoz reviews each family summary and sets the recommendation. She signs the report. Legal conclusions are hers.

blocks.text: Limits
This is a review. It does not include new filings, office action responses, or validity and infringement opinions.
Some families will look like continuation candidates. Take those to Heather Munoz with a rough cost first. The client hears the cost in the same message as the suggestion.
Ground Rules

items: Client contact goes through me. Heather Munoz approves anything that carries a recommendation before it goes out.
One issues list per family, kept in the matter folder. Close an issue only with a note of how it closed.
Record time to the matter as usual. The fee is fixed, but we need to know what the review costs us.
Mark every family summary privileged and confidential. The client may circulate the report internally, so draft for that reader.

blocks.text: Known Risks

items: The client's docket may not match office records. Treat the office records as correct until shown otherwise.
Some inventors may have left the company. Their agreements decide whether title can be fixed without new signatures.
Product information may lag the claims work. Map only against descriptions the client has confirmed as current.
Scope drift. Whether a product is clear to sell is a freedom-to-operate question. It goes to Heather Munoz, not into the review.

blocks.text: Before the End of Next Week

items: Today: I send Gary Smith the document request. It covers the docket export, file copies, inventor agreements, and the current product list.
Sharon Woods opens the matter on our docket and starts the reconciliation as the export arrives.
Amanda Schwartz pulls the USPTO assignment records for every family and opens the issues list.
I set up the family index in the matter folder. One row per family. One owner per row.
Team check-in each Monday, fifteen minutes, until the reconciliation closes.

blocks.text: Anything that touches a deadline comes to Sharon Woods and me the same day. Everything else waits for Monday.
Gary,

This thread will carry our updates on the portfolio review. The docket reconciliation is finished, and your records match the patent office records on every open deadline. Amanda Schwartz, the associate on our team, has started the title review, and I am working through the families in deadline order.

One item cannot wait for its turn. An older issued patent is inside its maintenance fee window, and the window closes before the review would reach that family. Heather Munoz, the partner supervising the review, will send you her recommendation on it this week. No action is needed from you until then.

Three items from {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} would keep the work moving:
1. Signed assignment or employment agreements for the inventors on the older families. The recorded assignments are incomplete for some of them. Copies are fine for now.
2. Your current product list.
3. The name of whoever handles foreign annuity payments, if that is not you.
A caveat on all of this. The reconciliation shows what the records say. It does not yet show which patents are worth keeping. That comes with the family review.
Best,
Dear Gary,
My recommendation is to pay the maintenance fee on the older patent now. Decide its long-term value when the review reaches its family.

The reasons, in order:
1. Paying keeps the patent in force for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}. It commits you to nothing beyond this payment.
2. The fee is a published official fee. Under our engagement letter it is billed at cost.
3. A lapsed patent can sometimes be revived by petition. The petition requires a statement that the delay was unintentional, and a deliberate decision to wait would not support that statement.
We pay maintenance fees only on your written instruction. A reply to this message is enough. Kelly Snyder will confirm to you once the payment is recorded.
Of the three items Kelly Snyder asked for, the inventor agreements come first. The title review cannot close without them.
Best,

blocks.text: Working Session Minutes: Patent Portfolio Review for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}

The issued families reviewed so far are in workable order, and the review stays on its current schedule. Three decisions were taken. They are recorded below, followed by the discussion and the open items.
Present

items: Heather Munoz, Partner
Kelly Snyder, Patent Agent
Amanda Schwartz, Associate
Gary Smith, General Manager, {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}

blocks.text: Decisions

items: Corrective assignments go ahead on the older families with gaps in the recorded title.
No continuation is filed until Gary Smith has a cost estimate for it.
Lapse candidates stay in force until the final report. Any payment that falls due first comes to Gary Smith with a recommendation well ahead of its date.

blocks.text: Discussion

Issued families. Kelly Snyder took the group through the issued families finished so far. Most are in force, with clean prosecution histories and claims that still read on products in the current list.
Some cover products the company no longer sells. Those are the lapse candidates. Gary Smith asked that none be dropped before he has seen the final report.

Title. Amanda Schwartz reported that several older families lack a recorded assignment from at least one inventor. If the inventor's employment agreement contains a present assignment of inventions, recording that agreement may close the gap; if it only promises a future assignment, a signed assignment is needed.
Gary Smith will find out which of those inventors are still with the company. For anyone who has left, Amanda Schwartz will set out the options in writing.

Pending applications. One pending family has subject matter that may be worth a continuation. A continuation must be filed while the parent is still pending, so the family is flagged on our docket while the estimate is prepared.
Kelly Snyder noted that the filing and prosecution costs of a continuation sit outside this review. Gary Smith asked for the estimate before any decision.

Foreign counterparts. Gary Smith confirmed that his office pays the foreign annuities directly. Kelly Snyder will send him the annuity dates from the reconciliation so that both calendars carry the same dates.
Maintenance fee. The fee paid in June on the older patent is recorded. That family will be reviewed in its turn, like the others.
Products. The current product list is mapped. Planned releases are not, because the release plans have not yet arrived.
Schedule. The remaining families follow in deadline order. Kelly Snyder will circulate a written status report later this month.
Open Items

rows: Confirm which inventors on the older families are still employed and locate their agreements
Send the foreign annuity dates from the reconciliation
Send release plans for the next two years
Draft corrective assignments for the families with recording gaps
Within two weeks of receiving the agreements
Prepare a cost estimate for the continuation candidate
Review the lapse candidates and approve each recommendation
